```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(OmicsChrono))
```

# Introduction

Longitudinal and circadian studies often describe sample time using a mixture
of elapsed durations, civil timestamps, subject-specific baselines, and light
cycle coordinates. These quantities have different meanings. In particular,
civil clock readings may be ambiguous or nonexistent around daylight-saving
transitions, while replicate samples may not land exactly on planned sampling
windows.

OmicsChrono is an upstream metadata layer for making these temporal
assumptions explicit in `SummarizedExperiment` and its derived classes. It
stores sample annotations in `colData()` and does not read or alter assay
values. The result is suitable for downstream modeling workflows that expect
an explicit temporal design.

## Relationship to existing Bioconductor software

Several Bioconductor packages analyze temporal biological measurements:

| Package | Main temporal task | OmicsChrono's boundary |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `rain` | Non-parametric detection of rhythmic patterns in time series | Validates sample-time metadata before measurements are modeled |
| `DiscoRhythm` | Rhythm detection and exploratory/quality-control visualizations | Represents civil and experimental time and reports sampling coverage |
| `timeOmics` | Integration and clustering of longitudinal multi-omics profiles | Standardizes sample-level time metadata without fitting profiles |
| `Rnits`, `splineTimeR`, `TMixClust`, `timecourse` | Time-course rhythm, spline, clustering, or developmental-series analyses | Does not duplicate statistical models; supplies checked design inputs |

These tools address downstream analysis of biological signal. OmicsChrono
addresses the preceding data-engineering step: checking what each sample's time
means and whether the observed design matches its stated schedule. Package
scope is limited to metadata; it does not identify rhythmic genes or estimate
molecular phase.

# Real RNA-seq time-course data

The `fission` experiment-data package supplies a `RangedSummarizedExperiment`
of fission yeast RNA-seq samples collected at 0, 15, 30, 60, 120, and 180
minutes after oxidative stress, in wild-type and `atf21`-deletion strains.
These are elapsed experimental minutes rather than civil timestamps.

```{r fission}
data("fission", package = "fission")
fission
```

Inspect sample-level metadata and the planned time points:

```{r inspect-fission}
cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(fission)
names(cd)
sort(unique(cd$minute))
fission_subject <- paste(cd$strain, cd$replicate, sep = "_")
## Rebuild the packaged snapshot with the current assay wrapper while retaining
## its real counts, genomic ranges, and sample annotations.
fission_current <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = SummarizedExperiment::assay(fission)),
    rowRanges = SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(fission),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(as.data.frame(cd))
)
```

Validate the minute column and annotate hours from the first sample. The
sample order is preserved; if the order is not chronological, the validation
report records that fact rather than reordering samples.

```{r annotate-fission}
validation <- validateSampleTime(
    fission_current, time = "minute", subject = fission_subject, time_unit = "minutes"
)
validation

fission_timed <- annotateSampleTime(
    fission_current, time = "minute", subject = fission_subject, time_unit = "minutes"
)
head(SummarizedExperiment::colData(fission_timed)[,
    c("minute", "chrono_elapsed_hours", "chrono_sampling_interval_hours")])
```

Summarize the available time points by strain and check one-to-one alignment
for a single strain. Replicate measurements remain separate observations and
are never combined or modified by alignment.

```{r coverage-fission}
temporalCoverage(
    fission_timed,
    time = "chrono_elapsed_hours",
    subject = fission_subject,
    condition = "strain"
)

wt <- cd$strain == "wt" & cd$replicate == "r1"
alignSampleTimes(
    observed = as.numeric(as.character(cd$minute[wt])),
    expected = c(0, 15, 30, 60, 120, 180),
    tolerance = 0.01,
    sample = colnames(fission)[wt]
)
```

The container's structure and assay values are preserved:

```{r preservation-fission}
class(fission)
class(fission_timed)
    identical(dim(fission_current), dim(fission_timed))
identical(colnames(fission_current), colnames(fission_timed))
identical(SummarizedExperiment::assay(fission_current),
          SummarizedExperiment::assay(fission_timed))
identical(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(fission_current),
          SummarizedExperiment::rowData(fission_timed))
```

# Civil timestamps and daylight saving

The following tiny example is synthetic and is used only to illustrate civil
time behavior. A timestamp string such as `2024-10-27 02:30:00` in
`Europe/Oslo` occurs twice when clocks move back. The default diagnostic does
not silently choose one instant. The analyst can explicitly select the first
or second occurrence after reviewing the experiment's collection records.

```{r synthetic-dst}
synthetic <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = matrix(c(3L, 7L), nrow = 1,
                                  dimnames = list("gene1", c("sample1", "sample2")))),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        collection_time = c("2024-10-27 02:30:00", "2024-10-27 03:30:00"),
        timezone = c("Europe/Oslo", "Europe/Oslo")
    )
)
validateSampleTime(
    synthetic, "collection_time", timezone = synthetic$timezone
)
resolved <- annotateSampleTime(
    synthetic, "collection_time", timezone = synthetic$timezone,
    ambiguous = "earliest"
)
SummarizedExperiment::colData(resolved)[,
    c("chrono_timestamp_utc", "chrono_timestamp_local", "chrono_is_dst")]
```

For a spring-forward gap, the local time does not exist. It is reported as
`nonexistent_local_time` and cannot be converted:

```{r spring-gap}
spring_gap <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = matrix(1L, nrow = 1)),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(collection_time = "2024-03-31 02:30:00")
)
validateSampleTime(spring_gap, "collection_time", timezone = "Europe/Oslo")
```

# Zeitgeber time and photoperiod

In a controlled light schedule, ZT0 is the supplied lights-on time. This is
metadata transformation based on the experimental protocol; OmicsChrono does
not infer circadian phase from gene expression.

```{r zeitgeber}
light_study <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = matrix(1:3, nrow = 1)),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        collection_time = c("2024-06-01 07:00:00",
                            "2024-06-01 18:00:00",
                            "2024-06-01 20:00:00")
    )
)
light_study <- addZeitgeberTime(
    light_study, "collection_time", lights_on = "07:00",
    timezone = "Europe/Oslo", photoperiod = 12
)
SummarizedExperiment::colData(light_study)[,
    c("chrono_zeitgeber_hours", "chrono_light_phase",
      "chrono_hours_until_phase_change")]
```

# Analysis-ready design data

When cyclical covariates are useful to a downstream method, the cycle length
must be supplied explicitly. The helper returns sample-level covariates in
input order and does not fit a statistical model.

```{r design-data}
design <- temporalDesignData(
    fission_timed, time = "chrono_elapsed_hours", condition = "strain",
    cycle_length = 24
)
head(design)
```

# Limitations

* Civil timestamp parsing accepts local ISO timestamps to whole seconds and
  requires an IANA time zone. Numeric offsets embedded in strings are not
  interpreted; convert them to an absolute `POSIXct` instant first.
* A daylight-saving repeated time is ambiguous without an offset, fold marker,
  or collection record. OmicsChrono reports the ambiguity and never assumes
  which occurrence was intended.
* Time-zone rules describe civil time; they do not model experimental clock
  drift or deviations in an animal facility's light controller.
* Zeitgeber annotation uses a supplied local lights-on time and a 24-hour
  cycle. It does not discover phase, periodicity, or rhythmicity.
* Alignment reports metadata correspondence only. It does not impute missing
  assay measurements or change sample order.
